questions.q:
Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of

$\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11)) + 10 \sin\left(2 \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right) + 10 \sin(2 \tan^{-1}(2))$

is
questions.solution:
For the first term, $\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11))$:
The principal value branch of $\cot^{-1}(x)$ is $(0, \pi)$.
Since the cotangent function is periodic with period $\pi$, $\cot(-11) = \cot(-11 + 4\pi)$.
Using $\pi \approx 3.14$, we have $4\pi \approx 12.56$, so $-11 + 4\pi \approx 1.56$, which lies in the interval $(0, \pi)$.
Thus, $\cot^{-1}(\cot(-11)) = 4\pi - 11$.

For the second term, $10 \sin\left(2 \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\right)$:
Since $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, we get:
$10 \sin\left(2 \times \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 10 \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 10(1) = 10$.

For the third term, $10 \sin(2 \tan^{-1}(2))$:
Let $\theta = \tan^{-1}(2) \Rightarrow \tan(\theta) = 2$.
Using the multiple angle formula $\sin(2\theta) = \dfrac{2\tan(\theta)}{1 + \tan^2(\theta)}$, we obtain:
$\sin(2\theta) = \dfrac{2(2)}{1 + 2^2} = \dfrac{4}{5}$.
Therefore, $10 \sin(2 \tan^{-1}(2)) = 10 \times \dfrac{4}{5} = 8$.

Adding the three evaluated terms together:
$(4\pi - 11) + 10 + 8 = 4\pi + 7$.

Answer: $4\pi + 7$

questions.q: Considering only the principal values of the inverse trigonometric functions, the value of $\tan \left(\sin ^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)-2 \cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Let $E = \tan\left(\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) - 2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)\right)$.

Evaluate the inverse trigonometric expressions: Let $\alpha = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)$, so $\sin\alpha = \frac{3}{5}$ and $\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}$. Let $\beta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$, so $\cos\beta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ and $\tan\beta = \frac{1}{2}$.

Compute the double angle: Using $\tan(2\beta) = \frac{2\tan\beta}{1 - \tan^2\beta}$, we obtain $\tan(2\beta) = \frac{2\cdot\frac{1}{2}}{1 - \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{4}{3}$.

Apply the tangent subtraction formula: $E = \tan(\alpha - 2\beta) = \frac{\tan\alpha - \tan(2\beta)}{1 + \tan\alpha\tan(2\beta)} = \frac{\frac{3}{4} - \frac{4}{3}}{1 + \frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{3}} = \frac{-\frac{7}{12}}{2} = -\frac{7}{24}$.

Final result: $\boxed{-\frac{7}{24}}$

questions.q:
For any positive integer $n$, let ${S}_{n}: ( 0, \infty ) \to R$ be defined by
${S}_{n}\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 + k ( k + 1 ) {x}^{2}}{x}\right)$
where for any $x \in R, {cot}^{- 1} ( x ) \in ( 0, \pi )$ and $\tan^{- 1} ( x ) \in \left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$. Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: The equation ${S}_{3} ( x ) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ has a root in $( 0, \infty )$
questions.solution:
${S}_{n}\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 + k ( k + 1 ) {x}^{2}}{x}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}{cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 + kx ( k + 1 ) x}{( k + 1 ) x - kx}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{( k + 1 ) x - kx}{1 + kx ( k + 1 ) x}\right)$

$= \mathop{∑}_{k = 1}^{n}\left[\tan^{- 1} ( k + 1 ) x - \tan^{- 1}kx\right]$

$= \left[\tan^{- 1} ( n + 1 ) x - \tan^{- 1}nx\right] + \ldots + \left[\tan^{- 1}3x - \tan^{- 1}2x\right] + \left[\tan^{- 1}2x - \tan^{- 1}x\right]$

$= \tan^{- 1} ( n + 1 ) x - \tan^{- 1}x$

$= \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{( n + 1 ) x - x}{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}\right)$

$= \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{nx}{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}\right)$

1. ${S}_{10}\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{10x}{1 + 11{x}^{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{2} - {cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{10x}{1 + 11{x}^{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 + 11{x}^{2}}{10x}\right)$

2. $\lim_{n \to \infty}cot\left({S}_{n} ( x )\right) = \lim_{n \to \infty}cot\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{nx}{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}\right)\right)$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}cot\left({cot}^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}{nx}\right)\right)$

$= \lim_{n \to \infty}\left(\dfrac{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}{nx}\right)$

$= \dfrac{{x}^{2}}{x} = x$

3. ${S}_{3}\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{3x}{1 + 4{x}^{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{3x}{1 + 4{x}^{2}}\right) = tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$⇒ \dfrac{3x}{1 + 4{x}^{2}} = 1$

$⇒ 1 + 4{x}^{2} = 3x$

$⇒ 4{x}^{2} - 3x + 1 = 0$

$D < 0$

Hence, no real roots.

4. $tan\left({S}_{n} ( x )\right) = tan\left(\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{nx}{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}\right)\right) = \left(\dfrac{nx}{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}\right)$

$\left(\dfrac{nx}{1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}}\right) \le \dfrac{1}{2} ⇒ 2nx \le 1 + ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2}$

$⇒ 2nx \le ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2} + 1$

$⇒ ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2} - 2nx + 1 \ge 0 ∀ n \ge 1; x > 0$

Let, $y = ( n + 1 ) {x}^{2} - 2nx + 1$

$D = 4{n}^{2} - 4 ( n + 1 )$ and $n \in N$

$D < 0$ for $n = 1$

Hence, no solution if $n = 1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
For any positive integer $n$, define ${f}_{n}: \left(0, \infty\right) \to R$ as

${f}_{n}\left(x\right) = {∑}_{i = 1}^{n}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + \left(x + j\right)\left(x + j - 1\right)}\right)$ for all $x \in \left(0, \infty\right)$ .

$($Here, the inverse trigonometric function $\tan^{- 1} ⁡ x$ assumes values in $\left(- \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$$)$

Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
questions.solution:
${f}_{n}\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{j = 1}^{n}\tan^{- 1}\left(\dfrac{\left(x + j\right) - \left(x + j - 1\right)}{1 + \left(x + j\right)\left(x + j - 1\right)}\right)$ ${f}_{n}\left(x\right) = \mathop{∑}_{j = 1}^{n}\left[\tan^{- 1}\left(x + j\right) - \tan^{- 1}\left(x + j - 1\right)\right]$
${f}_{n}\left(x\right) = \tan^{- 1}\left(x + n\right) - \tan^{- 1}x$
$∴$ $tan\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = tan\left[\tan^{- 1}\left(x + n\right) - \tan^{- 1}x\right]$

$tan\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = tan\left[\tan^{- 1}\dfrac{\left(x + n\right) - x}{1 + x\left(x + n\right)}\right]$
$tan\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = \dfrac{n}{1 + {x}^{2} + nx}$,

so that $\lim_{x \to \infty}tan\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = 0$
$∴$ ${sec}^{2}\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = 1 + \tan^{2}\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right)$
${sec}^{2}\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = 1 + {\left(\dfrac{n}{1 + {x}^{2} + nx}\right)}^{2}$
$\lim_{x \to \infty}{sec}^{2}\left({f}_{n}\left(x\right)\right) = \lim_{x \to \infty}1 + {\left(\dfrac{n}{1 + {x}^{2} + nx}\right)}^{2} = 1$

Note that since $0$ is not in domain so first two options are wrong

questions.q: If $0 < x < 1$, then $\sqrt{1+x^2}\left[\left\{x \cos \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)+\sin \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)\right\}^2-1\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
We have, $0 < x < 1$ Let $\quad \cot ^{-1} x=\theta$ $\Rightarrow \quad \cot \theta=x$ $\therefore \quad \sin \theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}=\sin \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)$ and $\quad \cos \theta=\frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}=\cos \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)$ Now, $\sqrt{1+x^2}\left[\left\{x \cos \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)+\sin \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)\right\}^2-1\right]^{1 / 2}$
$$ \text{ Now, } \begin{aligned} & \sqrt{1+x^2}\left[\left\{x \cos \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)+\sin \left(\cot ^{-1} x\right)\right\}^2-1\right]^{1 / 2} \\ &=\sqrt{1+x^2}\left[\left\{x \frac{x}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\right\}^2-1\right]^{1 / 2} \\ &=\sqrt{1+x^2}\left[\left(\frac{1+x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\right)^2-1\right]^{1 / 2} \\ &=\sqrt{1+x^2}\left[1+x^2-1\right]^{1 / 2} \\ &=x \sqrt{1+x^2} \end{aligned} $$

questions.q: Let $(x, y)$ be such that $\sin ^{-1}(a x)+\cos ^{-1}(y)+\cos ^{-1}(b x y)=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Match the statements in Column I with the values in Column II.
options:
A-p; B-q; C-q; D-p

A-p; B-q; C-p; D-s

A-s; B-p; C-q; D-p

A-r; B-q; C-p; D-r
questions.solution:
(A) If $a=1 and b=0$, then $\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} y=0 $
\Rightarrow \quad \sin ^{-1} x=-\cos ^{-1} y \Rightarrow x^2+y^2=1
 
(B) If $a=1 and b=1$, then
 $\begin{array}{rlrl} 
& & \sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1} y+\cos ^{-1} x y & =\frac{\pi}{2} \\
\Rightarrow & & \cos ^{-1} x-\cos ^{-1} y & =\cos ^{-1} x y \\
\Rightarrow & x y+\sqrt{1-x^2} \sqrt{1-y^2} & =x y \quad \text{ [taking sine on both$ the $sides] }
\end{array}$
(C) If $a=1 and b=2$, then
 \begin{aligned}
& & $\sin ^{-1} x+\cos$ ^{-1} y+$\cos ^{-1}$(2 x y) & =$\frac{\pi}{2}$ \\
\Rightarrow & & $\cos ^{-1} x-\cos$ ^{-1} y & =$\cos ^{-1}$(2 x y) \\
\Rightarrow & & x y+\sqrt{1-x^2} \sqrt{1-y^2} & =2 x y \\
\Rightarrow & & x^2+y^2 & =1
\end{aligned} 
[on squaring]
(D) If $a=2 and b=2$, then
 \begin{aligned}
& & $\sin ^{-1}$(2 x)+$\cos ^{-1}$(y)+$\cos ^{-1}$(2 x y) & =$\frac{\pi}{2}$ \\
\Rightarrow & & 2 x y+\sqrt{1+4 x^2} \sqrt{1-y^2} & =2 x y \\
\Rightarrow & & $\left(4 x^2-1\right) \left(y^2-1\right) & =0 .
\end{aligned} $
